contracts.selectedText:
**F-S01 — Source boundary.** Follow L-F01–L-F07 and F-P01–F-P06. The exact source root is the existing computer-system-engine package, bound by the generation inventory. Create only `src/journal/filesystem/source-owner.mjs` and `src/journal/diagnostics.mjs`; edit only `package.json` to add `./journal/filesystem/source-owner` and `./journal/diagnostics` exports to those paths. Preserve all existing package fields and exports. No dependency additions, operational data writes by the generator, new framework, alternate codec, permanent index, sidecar authority or Code-to-System import. The inventory binds the package bytes and absent targets before invocation. Read-only source inputs provide existing laws, not authority to preserve old storage machinery.


**F-S07 — Required evidence and existing-source durability.** Implement L-O26–L-O28's closure, longest causal path, exact semantic byte charges, sufficient physical custody cover and opaque per-scope barrier evidence. Source synchronization must use the same verified descriptors, include mandatory original unique occupancy, and synchronize required directory entries bottom-up through the filesystem root. Bind every name and ancestor; do not assume O_NOFOLLOW on the final file validates its parent path. Recheck required bytes even on cache hits. A successful existing-source barrier neither republishes evidence nor creates staging files, and common duplicate site bodies must not force synchronization of unrelated history. Do not add an alternate closure codec, interpret arbitrary embedded strings as edges, or require fabricated envelopes for core-only causal evidence.


**F-S08 — Independent receiving responsibility.** The source provider returns a candidate from this public contract and exact supplied bytes, with no tool access and no private receiving material. It is not asked to execute or certify future acceptance. Refuse only for a specific missing/contradictory source requirement or inability to supply the implementation, not because the intentionally isolated provider cannot run the assessor. The independent operator commits private fixtures before generation, materializes the closed patchset, syntax-checks the staged files and runs it in a network-denied namespace with only required dependencies and fixture directories. No credentials or operational corpus enter receiving. Review source for binding/descriptor cleanup, budget enforcement, gate lifetime, private diagnostic leakage, uncertainty handling and custody correspondence even if fixtures pass. No assessor behavioral repair or private-feedback retry is permitted.

Receiving must demonstrate initialization/retry/conflict, unchanged identities across reopen, same-process and separate-process exclusion, scope expiry and callback error preservation, ordinary/unique shared discovery, original command-payload recovery, duplicate/conflicting requests, pending-to-admitted recovery, retained blocks, membership-only additions, exact selections and accounting, source withdrawal/corruption, changed root/host/lock refusal, configured resource refusals and actual required-source synchronization with failure injection. Further integration receiving must establish all L-O06 consumer effects and legacy retirement before the replacement is called complete. A finite fixture set alone does not prove all host/production properties.


**F-S09 — Evidence and promotion boundary.** Record the exact specification/dependency/input/assay/candidate digests, requested and observed Luna model, executable/profile, namespace observation, invocation duration, measured tokens, and cash cost unavailable when not reported. The generation inventory and public source bundle are immutable during an invocation. Any unexpected provider tool activity or source change rejects it. A passing owner candidate remains a dependency, not an accepted operating application. Before any promotion recheck all protected bytes and absent targets and preserve exact originals; report partial multi-file promotion honestly. Do not remove the old writer or mutate a real journal in this dependency order. The connected facade/domain/consumer and offline migration patchset carries the retirement obligation.


**F-S11 — Two dependent source-generation stages.** The complete owner may be generated in two source calls after the first whole-owner provider declined to supply an implementation. This changes the source-call boundary, not the required final behavior, private receiving fixtures, source inventory or promotion condition. Both stages remain unaccepted outside the working repository until the combined result satisfies the complete order. The operator does not write or repair product behavior.

Stage A supplies the complete diagnostics module, package exports, explicit host initialization, immutable root/host binding, descriptor-owned gate and withOperation lifetime/error handling. Within source-owner.mjs it leaves exactly one designated private generation seam:

```js
function createSourceScope(operation) {
  throw new TypeError("journal source view fabrication incomplete");
}
```

This seam is an explicit staging-only incompleteness marker, never a runtime fallback and never promotable. withOperation calls it under the held gate before invoking the trusted callback. Its operation argument is a frozen private object containing exactly root (bound absolute directory), configuration (the deeply frozen admitted host configuration), cache (one owner-private mutable cell with property value, initially undefined), assertLive (throws outside this operation), assertBindings (rechecks current root/host/lock bindings), and markPublicationPossible (sets the operation's uncertainty flag irreversibly). Methods check the captured lifetime, not a caller-supplied flag. The argument is never returned or serialized. The host stage provides all actual initialization and host-boundary behavior; it does not pretend a source view exists.

Stage B receives the exact generated Stage-A bytes and the source-view specification/dependencies. It replaces that private seam with the complete source reader, scope methods, source-derived cache, publication and durability behavior; additional private helpers may be inserted within the same owner module. It may refine Stage-A private helper composition where necessary while preserving all host and diagnostic contracts. It removes the staging-only error and all placeholders. No public alternate constructor or partially functional scope survives. The final inventory retains the original checkout package digest and absent creation targets for eventual promotion; Stage-B staging edits are bound separately to the precise Stage-A source bytes.

Syntax and public source review may occur between stages; the complete committed private receiver runs only against the composed result after Stage B. Source-provider input includes only the clauses and dependency source needed for its stage, with hashes binding the full order and predecessor files. Private receiving outcomes are never sent to either provider. A refusal or failure preserves the incomplete stages as unaccepted evidence and does not authorize hand completion or a reduced acceptance claim.


**F-S15 — Separate source reconstruction from scope effects.** Stage-B attempt05 declined the remaining complete implementation even with the existing address API explicitly supplied. Split that unfinished source work into B1 and B2; this supersedes only F-S11's Stage-B invocation boundary. The final source inventory, required behavior and independent receiver remain unchanged. No intermediate phase is promoted or assessed as a working owner. All stages are generated in isolated fresh contexts; the operator supplies specifications and deterministic staging, never behavioral repairs.

B1 generates the bounded recognized-source discovery and verified derived view only. Add private `refreshSourceView(operation)` and its necessary private helpers to the staged source-owner.mjs. Keep the exact createSourceScope incompleteness seam and all existing host code unchanged except imports needed by B1. B1 is not responsible for resolving F-S13's existing host defects: B2 must correct them before complete receiving. Do not generate public scope methods, publication or fsync/barrier behavior in B1. The ordinary and unique source reader must itself satisfy F-S04/F-S10, L-O22/L-O23/L-O25/L-O26/L-O27's source-correspondence rule, and the existing wire/causal laws. Existing filesystem helper use remains in the host code; B1 performs bounded reads and derived-memory construction only.

`operation` is exactly the F-S11 private context. Call operation.assertLive and operation.assertBindings before reading and after reconstruction. The value returned by refreshSourceView is an internal record, never returned to a user or serialized. Its fields are:

| Field | Internal representation and meaning |
| --- | --- |
| substrate | The existing Code CausalSubstrate instance, obtained by unwrapping a successful rebuildCausalSubstrate/receiveSourceSet judgment |
| sources | Map from recognized root-relative final filename to `{name,kind,identity,size,digest,bytes,parsed}`; name is that key, kind is `retained` or `unique`, identity is frozen `{dev,ino}`, size is exact byte length, digest is SHA-256 of exact bytes, bytes is the private bounded Buffer, and parsed is the verified retained-entry array or parseUniqueJournalRecord result |
| envelopes | Map from event reference to `{statement,canonicalText}`, the normalized verified envelope and its canonical text; retain original verified values inside source parsed records |
| feedEvents | Map from admitted safe-feed string to Set of retained event references with that membership, regardless of current causal state |
| artifactCustody | Map from verified artifact reference to Set of recognized source names containing its exact body or L-O26's verified embedded command body |
| envelopeCustody | Map from event reference to Set of recognized source names containing its agreed normalized envelope |
| uniqueEntries | Map from slot digest to the authoritative parseUniqueJournalRecord result; a copied ordinary witness/body never supplies this map |
| historicalObstructions | Map from event reference to canonical-text-sorted, exact-deduplicated arrays of original verified retained obstruction JSON values, including falsy values and bodyless events |
| sourceFiles | Distinct recognized physical-source count under L-M03 |
| sourceBytes | Sum of exact lengths of those distinct physical sources under L-M03 |

The maps and Buffer are private derived state. They must not escape through future scope results; B2 copies/freezes public values according to L-O02. No method mutates the substrate's internal maps. The cache cell belongs to the owner. It may contain a private state record with the last complete view and the metadata necessary for L-O25's reuse. B1 installs a replacement cache value only after discovery/verification/reconstruction and final binding checks succeed. A partially processed source set is never installed as the current view. If mutable substrate receiveSourceSet would be used for a monotone update, ensure all new source records and correspondence/decision checks have passed before delivering the complete set of unseen bodies; invalidate the cache if a later failure leaves its derived judgment unsuitable for reuse. Do not build and discard a second complete substrate merely to claim warm reuse.

Discovery streams the root and exact source-family directories under F-S10. It rejects an unsupported root layout or corrupted recognized family rather than ignoring it. Bound current descriptor lengths and reads before allocation, close descriptors without masking the primary failure, bind nonsymlink parents and final names before/after reads, and enforce all corpus/discovery limits. Unique whole-record bytes retain the fixed JSON envelope; retained entries use L-O23's line-derived envelope, while their artifact bodies and obstruction values retain their own smaller envelopes. Parsing canonical source bytes must compare the actual bytes to the required representation, not compare two normalized values. Retained batches require exact canonical sorted/deduplicated entry lines, LF, and filename/body digest agreement. A unique source requires canonical verified record plus LF and filename slot correspondence through the existing parser. No source read calls create-only publication or creates a missing directory.

For source mapping, verify each ordinary statement with parseJournalWitness, register its original source pairs as artifact custody, register its normalized envelope and feed membership, and detect normalized-envelope conflicts by event reference. Register standalone retained artifacts only after the existing artifact verifier succeeds. Collect historical decisions from retained obstruction entries before causal reconstruction, retaining exact original values. Unique records register their witness source pairs, explicit record artifacts, L-O26's addressed parsed command body, normalized envelope and F-S14's virtual feed. Duplicate body references must agree in canonical text; duplicate envelope references must agree in normalized canonical text. Duplicate physical custody must not inflate semantic counts or replace an original unique record.

On a cold view call rebuildCausalSubstrate with the complete unique verified source pairs and all current retained obstruction records in its fourth argument. Use the returned substrate, including its admission, quarantine and obstruction judgments; a retained blocked decision is not an owner-invented second evaluator. On a warm view, exact physical identities/digests and decisions establish the unchanged, monotone-addition or rebuild case in L-O25. Build membership and custody maps from every current record even when parsed/semantic verification is reused. A removed source invalidates its custody and unique occupancy contribution. A malformed changed source refuses; it does not behave like removal. Return private fields with the exact above meanings, leaving sourceStatus, events and the remaining public scope assembly to B2.

B2 receives the exact staged B1 bytes, the complete owner contracts and public F-S13 corrections. It replaces createSourceScope with the complete scope API using refreshSourceView, supplies protected publication and closure/barrier methods, completes host corrections, and removes every incompleteness marker. It may refactor B1's private representation only if every consumer is changed coherently in the same generated candidate; no obsolete adapter survives. Only this composed result is eligible for the unchanged complete receiver and final source review. Finishing B1 is source-generation progress, not storage or assistant acceptance.


**F-S19 — Generate remaining operations in dependency order.** Attempt14 supplied no B2 implementation. Decompose B2 into B2a (read scope), B2b (required-evidence barrier and host corrections), and B2c (publication and final composition). This changes only the invocation boundary. The complete owner contract, writable inventory, final independent receiver and connected migration/retirement obligations remain unchanged. Do not interpret a partial stage as a usable or accepted owner. Generate all behavioral source in isolated contexts from the existing specifications and exact preceding staged bytes.

B2a replaces createSourceScope's single incompleteness seam with the live, frozen read scope. Implement witness, artifact, feeds, events, sourceStatus, sourceUsage and uniqueRecord under L-O01/L-O02/L-O05/L-O22/L-O24/L-M01–L-M03. Use the complete existing refreshSourceView and the existing Code topological/causal laws. Complete read selections before exposing any envelopes, preserve core-only and bodyless-block observations, and enforce full-root required causal readiness for as-of before feed intersection. Preserve exact root-relative feed/date/frontier laws and descriptor-safe closed input admission. Do not add a second source scanner, causal evaluator or writable lookup. Public scope fields are exactly the ten methods: witness, artifact, feeds, events, sourceStatus, sourceUsage, uniqueRecord, publishRetained, publishUnique, requireDurable. The owner itself still exposes only withOperation.

For dependent composition, createSourceScope constructs private state `{operation,view}` where operation is the existing F-S11 context and view is the current refreshSourceView result. Brand the scope privately and retain this state only inside owner-private closures/WeakMap; no state/view/refresh method is public. All methods check the captured operation lifetime. Read methods use the current state.view, not a stale lexical copy; later publication must replace it with the refreshed complete view. Internal helper names may be chosen by generation, but B2a must define the three exact effect boundaries `publishRetainedInScope(state, entries)`, `publishUniqueInScope(state, record)` and `requireDurableInScope(state, requirement)`. Each has only the explicit incompleteness behavior of throwing TypeError with the fixed message `journal source effects fabrication incomplete`. The scope's corresponding methods perform the lifetime check and delegate to these private boundaries. These deliberate temporary seams are forbidden in final B2c. They supply no publication, durability or authorization success.

B2a preserves existing host functions and the reviewed physical/reconstruction paths except necessary imports and coherent private scope integration. F-S13 host corrections remain explicitly assigned to B2b; B2a does not claim them complete. Read results are deeply immutable and carry the exact prescribed shapes, with canonical body text retained as encoded document text rather than admitted again as one artifact string. Do not impose an artifact envelope on a retained normalized witness container; use its already verified source-derived value or the admitted line capacity when a snapshot is required. Internal source failures retain the closed diagnostic boundary, while malformed programmer input throws TypeError before mutation. No complete receiver runs against the deliberate seams.

B2b receives the exact staged B2a bytes. Replace requireDurableInScope with all L-O04/L-O26–L-O28 closure, longest causal path, exact witness/artifact charges, sufficient physical custody selection and existing-descriptor/ancestor barriers. Bind opaque receipts privately to the captured scope epoch and exact closure. Implement F-S13 host/init/cleanup/uncertainty corrections, using the same bound-descriptor barrier for initializeJournal's verified host/lock and ancestor custody. Preserve both publication seams and all read effects. It remains unaccepted and is not run through the complete receiver while those seams exist.

B2c receives that exact staged result. Implement publishRetainedInScope and publishUniqueInScope under L-O03/L-O05/F-S06, including descriptor-safe complete preflight, exact canonical source correspondence, source/discovery capacity, protected create-only publication, current-view refresh, correct new-retention/new-admission deltas, original occupied unique resolution and conservative publication uncertainty through final cleanup. Finish coherent composition and remove every fabrication-incomplete seam, temporary adapter, competing source path and obsolete helper. Only the resulting complete owner is eligible for the unchanged independent receiver and final source review. No production domain route, license selection, package release or completed assistant claim is introduced by these phases.


**F-S20 — Separate semantic custody selection from the physical barrier.** Attempt17 returned no B2b source. Realize its existing obligations in two dependent source transformations, B2b1 and B2b2, without weakening F-S19 or treating either as a released owner.

B2b1 generates the private `requiredSourceClosure(state, requirement)` helper from L-O04/L-O26–L-O28. It admits the exact descriptor-safe closed requirement and ordinal distinct dense reference arrays, verifies configured unique-slot identity and original occupancy, expands admitted event causes and required artifact bodies using the existing Code laws, enforces all semantic count/byte/longest-path bounds, and selects the deterministic sufficient custody cover. Return only private deeply immutable planning data with exactly `{journal, events, artifacts, sources}`: journal is the configured identity, events/artifacts are ordinal sorted reference arrays, and sources is an ordinal sorted array of selected root-relative final source names. Preserve every selected name even when several names share one physical identity; the next barrier deduplicates actual synchronization by verified device/inode while checking each name. Use the current verified view's source records and custody maps for selection; no independent scanner, evaluator, file, write, durable receipt or public method is added. The helper checks the captured operation lifetime and bindings. It may be defined before physical composition; requireDurableInScope and both publication helpers retain their explicit incompleteness behavior in this intermediate stage.

B2b2 consumes those exact source bytes and replaces requireDurableInScope with the bound-descriptor/ancestor barrier and scope-private opaque receipt, using requiredSourceClosure and the current view to bind the complete semantic sets and selected source identities/digests. It also completes every F-S13 host/init/cleanup/uncertainty correction as required by F-S19. B2c remains the full publication composition and removal of all seams. Only the complete owner receives final independent acceptance; no intermediate helper or syntax check proves durability.

The existing published Code export `@red-cup-engineering/computer-code-engineering-services-section/semiotic-eavt/identity/primitive-articulation` supplies addressPrimitiveArticulation. Resolve it to the already bound existing source file; do not duplicate that law or add a dependency. Before B2b1 generation, extend the receiving dependency map by that verified public export and recommit the map; the receiving program, loader, fixtures, assertions and file mounts remain byte-identical. This is dependency availability, not feedback from executing a candidate.


**F-S22 — Isolate existing-source synchronization from host repair.** Attempt21 supplied no B2b2 source. Generate B2b2a as the physical implementation of L-O28 and composition with the already reviewed requiredSourceClosure. It introduces a private reusable existing-file barrier and replaces requireDurableInScope; the two publication seams remain. This phase leaves all host initialization, gate, scanner and cleanup functions unchanged. B2b2b subsequently applies every F-S13 host correction using that same barrier, without claiming that B2b2a alone repairs the host or completes acceptance.

The private barrier accepts a bound absolute root, expected existing file descriptions and a caller-provided binding assertion. Descriptions identify root-relative nonsymlink regular files and their expected device/inode. Source and host descriptions also carry bounded exact previously verified bytes/digest and length; a stable maintenance-lock description can supply its already held descriptor without inventing semantic content or transferring descriptor ownership. It checks each named binding, reads bounded bytes from the verified descriptor, requires exact previous bytes/digest, and synchronizes selected physical files once while preserving all selected aliases for final checks. It holds and verifies the relevant ancestor directory descriptors before opening under them, synchronizes unique directories bottom-up through `/`, and rechecks named/held identities and caller bindings before success. Never create, publish, replace or delete anything. Close every descriptor it owns; preserve any primary thrown value using a separate failure flag, and surface a lone cleanup failure through the closed host diagnostic. Caller-owned descriptors remain open. The publication-uncertainty precedence still belongs to the protected outer operation and is completed in B2b2b/B2c.

requireDurableInScope invokes requiredSourceClosure, obtains the exact selected records from the current private view, runs that existing-source barrier, and stores the successful journal/semantic-reference/physical-source evidence privately behind a frozen opaque scope-bound receipt. It rechecks the live scope/bindings before acknowledgment. No serializable durable flag or public receipt validator is added. The private plan is never returned as proof of synchronization. Full L-O28 coverage and immutable independent receiving remain required after composition.

For this focused generation, supply exact excerpts containing the existing imports, required private helper definitions and the requireDurableInScope target, plus all top-level declaration names to prevent collisions. Bind each excerpt to its full file digest, original byte position and exact text; verify its occurrence before generation. The complete source file and ordinary F-P inventory stay bound and protected, and the unchanged materializer still resolves replacements against the entire file. Omit unrelated read-only dependency source and unrelated host-repair clauses from this invocation. This projection reduces input volume; it grants no authority to rewrite omitted code, extend the writable inventory or relax acceptance.

## L-O04 — Closure durability

The scope's `requireDurable({events, artifacts, uniqueSlot})` accepts ordinal distinct verified reference sets; uniqueSlot is either null or the exact closed `{journal, slotDigest}`. Journal must equal this protected owner's configured identity; slotDigest is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters obtained from `addressUniqueJournalCommand` or a verified parsed occupied record. The owner derives `unique-admissions/v1/<slotDigest>.json` itself, parses its exact bytes with `parseUniqueJournalRecord(value, journal, slotDigest)`, and includes that original record's witness and full required closure even if events/artifacts omit them. Unknown or unverified occupancy is evidence-unavailable. No caller-supplied pathname or serialized parsed result stands in for reading that authoritative slot. It expands the full required causal/artifact closure, verifies semantic state and exact source bytes, and synchronizes every required source and directory through the admitted ancestor barrier. Shared files are synchronized once; every required semantic reference remains represented. Exceeding any configured count/byte/depth budget is resource-limit; unresolved or blocked required material is evidence-unavailable. A digest-cache hit cannot stand in for a durability barrier.

The success value is opaque internal barrier evidence privately bound to this scope epoch and the complete sorted event/artifact/source-digest sets plus journal identity. No boolean `durable` argument or serialized prior receipt can replace it. It cannot be reused after gate release or for a different closure. Source publication for pending evidence uses the create-only helper's source-custody durability, not a forged successful admitted-closure result. Maintenance receipt/inventory sources likewise require their actual bytes durable before deletion; they are not required to invent admitted witness relationships for every historical pending item.

A facade returns a durable admission acknowledgment only after its requested admitted closure barrier succeeds. If source publication might be visible but the refresh/barrier/final binding check fails, return publication-uncertain as required by L-J06. Preserve visible bytes and permit later verified recovery; never remove them to imply rollback. For an already occupied unique slot, barrier the original retained command and its closure, not the conflicting proposed command.


## L-O28 — Existing-source barrier and sufficient physical custody

Derive the existing-source barrier from L-S07: acknowledging previously retained evidence requires synchronizing that evidence, not attempting to publish it again. The accepted `writeFileAtomicNew(..., {durable:true})` remains the create-only publication primitive. Its private synchronization helpers are not an available owner API, and its EEXIST branch is not a substitute for a read-only closure barrier. Implement a private Systems owner operation that opens existing required regular sources without following symlinks, verifies the descriptor against discovery, reads bounded exact bytes and rechecks their source digest/record correspondence, synchronizes the same descriptor, then synchronizes verified containing directories bottom-up through the filesystem root. Close every descriptor on success or failure. The barrier creates no file, staging sibling, source copy, receipt file or replacement directory.

Choose sufficient custody deterministically rather than synchronizing every duplicate of a common site/artifact throughout unrelated history. Start with the authoritative unique-slot file when requested. Process required event references in ordinal order: use a verified already-selected source containing the agreed normalized envelope, or the core body when core-only; otherwise select the ordinal-first root-relative recognized source name that supplies that representation. Then process required artifact references in ordinal order, retaining an already-selected supplying source when available and otherwise choosing the ordinal-first verified supplying source. Deduplicate selected physical files by their bound device/inode identity while retaining every selected source-name binding. This is a deterministic cover, not a claim to compute the globally smallest cover. Every required representation must have verified custody in the selected set. Unselected redundant copies still participate in the complete discovery/corruption checks required before this barrier.

Reread and verify selected sources even on parsed-cache hits. Recheck each selected name's binding to its open descriptor and the root/host/lock bindings before acknowledging. Synchronize each selected physical source once and each required directory once per barrier, in bottom-up order; the admitted host initialization barrier may discharge ancestors only under L-S07's exact unchanged binding. Maintain bounded provenance connecting every event/artifact representation to selected source bytes. A generic helper that follows an unchecked parent path does not establish this binding by itself.

The success result is a frozen opaque object with evidence retained in private scope-bound state, covering journal identity, sorted semantic reference sets and selected source digests/bindings. It has no serializable durability flag and expires with the operation. Missing required evidence, capacity refusal and host failures retain the existing reason vocabulary. A failure after publication may have become visible takes publication-uncertain precedence; the create-only helper supplies no reliable post-link stage marker, so do not infer rollback from its exception. Leave visible source bytes available for later recovery.

Receiving must establish successful re-acknowledgment from existing sources with no publication call or filesystem entry creation, complete semantic coverage despite deduplicated custody, mandatory original-slot synchronization, and no unrelated-history synchronization merely because a site body is duplicated there. Inject source/parent replacement and synchronization failure, including after possible publication, and observe refusal without rollback or reusable barrier evidence. These observations admit only the selected local host mechanism; they do not assert physical durability on unassessed deployment storage.

**L-S07 — Required closure barrier.** Starting from the candidate or occupied unique record, traverse its full required witness/artifact closure under the gate. Each resolved reference records the verified source file(s) containing its exact bytes. Deduplicate shared physical files; retain all semantic references in the internal barrier evidence. Synchronize every required source descriptor and directory entries bottom-up through the filesystem root as L-J07 requires. A verified root initialization barrier may discharge ancestors only under that exact unchanged root binding. A cache hit, inode existence or another closure's receipt is insufficient.

The internal successful evidence contains the configured journal identity, the sorted verified event/artifact references and the protected source content digests. It is returned only after every required synchronization succeeds. It grants no external dispatch permission and exposes no filesystem path in a public result. No closure file may be removed or replaced between verification and acknowledgment. Failure yields the L-J06 unavailable reason and retains already published bytes; it does not assert rollback.

## Necessary transformation

L-F02's exact-substring contract cannot create a System module or retire its superseded Code implementation. L-S06/L-S09 require both effects, including consumer migration. This order extends the deterministic materialization boundary for explicitly declared source creation and deletion. It does not add a scheduler, model harness, repository mutation service or product-code generator. Existing edit-only orders and their evidence remain unchanged. The source provider continues deriving behavioral source; the operator's deterministic materializer performs only declared byte transformations on a fresh staged directory.

**F-P01 — Opt-in input.** A patchset work order binds an exact source root and an input inventory. The inventory is a JSON object with exactly `kind`, `version`, `sourceRoot`, `files`, `clauses`. Kind is `source-patchset-input`; version is integer 1. SourceRoot is an absolute existing directory. Files is a path-keyed object. Every key is an admitted relative POSIX source path: nonempty components, each matching `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`, no dot/dot-dot component, absolute prefix, backslash or NUL. Each descriptor is exactly either `{state:"present",sha256}` or `{state:"absent"}`. Present entries bind lowercase SHA-256 of original bytes; absent entries authorize only creation. No path may be an ancestor of another admitted path. Clauses is a nonempty unique list of recognized nonempty clause-ID strings. Existing paths must be ordinary regular files and all existing ancestors, including the root's own path, must be nonsymlink directories; absent paths must also have no symlink or nondirectory ancestor. The inventory is trusted work-order input, not generated permission to touch files.

The concrete storage order must enumerate its exact writable files and clause IDs before source generation. This generic extension grants no writable source path by itself. Read-only dependencies and governing specification hashes remain protected under L-F01/L-F07 and are additional to this writable inventory.

**F-P02 — Closed candidate.** The new opt-in output is exactly `{kind:"source-patchset",version:1,disposition,reason,changes}`. Disposition is `candidate` or `refused`; reason is a string. A refusal has zero changes. A candidate has at least one change. Each admitted path occurs at most once, and every change contains a nonempty unique `clauses` array drawn from the inventory. No generated shell command, URL, dependency installation, permission change or recursive delete operation exists.

Changes are exactly one of:

- `{operation:"edit",path,inputSha256,replacements,clauses}` against a present entry. Each replacement is exactly `{before,after}`. Before is nonempty text occurring exactly once when that replacement is applied; after is text. Apply replacements in order against the original bound UTF-8 text. The one input digest remains the original file digest, not an intermediate value. The list is nonempty.
- `{operation:"create",path,text,clauses}` against an absent entry. Text is complete strict UTF-8 source, supplied by the generator; the operator must not fill behavioral placeholders. Creation emits an ordinary file with mode 0644. An executable entrypoint should normally be invoked through its existing runtime; changing execution bits requires a separately admitted order.
- `{operation:"delete",path,inputSha256,clauses}` against a present entry. This removes that exact file from the staged result. It does not delete directories, follow links, delete imports automatically or authorize removing unlisted data. Necessary consumer and export changes must appear as separately bound changes in the same work family.

All objects are closed. Reject Boolean values masquerading as integer versions, unknown operations, malformed digests, repeated paths, unknown clauses, invalid UTF-8, missing inputs, changed input bytes or an unexpectedly present creation target. Do not normalize generated paths or repair a refused candidate.

**F-P03 — Validate before staging.** The materializer rechecks every inventory entry, including unchanged inputs, before creating any staged output. It validates the whole candidate and calculates all intended output bytes in memory before writing. A malformed candidate therefore leaves no stage directory. It may inspect file metadata and bytes, but it never imports, evaluates or executes candidate text. The only mechanical transformations are the specified text replacements, creation and file omission.

Use a fresh nonexistent stage directory outside the source root. A stage ancestor cannot be a symlink or non-directory. The operator chooses that path; it is not accepted from the candidate. Copy each unchanged admitted present file and each resulting changed file into the stage at its declared relative path, preserving the existing file's permission bits for retained/edited files. Deleted inputs are omitted and their digests/modes retained in the receipt. Do not copy the repository's unbounded contents or leave links from the stage into the working checkout. Recheck all original inputs after staging before writing the staged result receipt. A concurrent change invalidates the stage and prevents acceptance; it does not authorize changing the concurrent work.

A host I/O error during staging may leave a partial staged directory. It must have no successful receipt; report failure and preserve it for inspection. Do not represent staging as an atomic multi-file filesystem transaction. A retry uses a fresh stage and fresh validation rather than overwriting an uncertain directory.

**F-P04 — Staged receipt and assessment.** The operator writes a sibling `<stage>.receipt.json` only after successful validation/staging/revalidation. The receipt contains kind `source-patchset-stage`, integer version 1, inventory/candidate digests, the materializer digest, each original path's presence/digest/mode, each final path's presence/digest/mode, and disposition `staged-unaccepted`. No receipt claims product acceptance or promotion. A receipt target already present refuses before staging; receipt creation is exclusive. A receipt write failure is a failed stage operation even if all source files have been written.

Independent assessment uses the exact staged tree plus explicitly admitted read-only dependencies. A retired file must be absent from that assessment namespace; a fallback mount of the old checkout must not make deleted code available again. Verify source creation, changed consumers and actual retired routes, not only that new files load. The private assessment remains excluded from source generation under L-F03–L-F05. Source provider and materializer receive no permission to amend acceptance fixtures after a failure.

**F-P05 — Promotion remains separate.** This materializer has no shared-checkout mutation or deployment mode. Product promotion remains governed by L-F07 plus the concrete work order's creation/deletion preconditions. Recheck all present/absent expectations before touching any target. Do not delete an obsolete file unless the complete affected capability and consumer migration have independently passed. A staged tree, deleted-path list or model assertion is insufficient. A multi-file promotion must record partial host failure accurately; it must not claim atomicity that the filesystem mechanism does not provide. Never restore over unrelated concurrent edits while trying to roll back a partial operation.

**F-P06 — Independent mechanical observations.** Demonstrate in disposable files that one batch creates a new file, changes an exact unique substring, retires a bound old file and carries an unchanged input, while leaving the source root byte-identical. Exercise stale/absent mismatch, ambiguous replacement, malformed/extra fields, repeated changes, unknown clause, path traversal, symlink input/ancestor, a path ancestor collision, malformed UTF-8 and an existing stage/receipt. Invalid input must produce no successful receipt or shared source mutation. The observations verify deterministic materialization only; they do not accept any journal or assistant behavior.

The initial realization may be a small operator-owned script retained with the fabrication evidence and invoked directly. It is not a new runtime package. This is mechanical tooling under the closed contract above; all product behavioral text in real candidates must still originate from the admitted isolated source-generation process.
